title: Equations and Inequalities
objectives: Understand and graph inequalities on number lines

introduction.context: Imagine you're planning a budget: 'If I spend x dollars on groceries and $30 on gas, and my total budget is $100, how much can I spend on groceries?' This is an equation waiting to be solved!
introduction.connection: Equations help us find unknown values in countless situations: calculating tips, determining travel time, balancing budgets, and solving engineering problems.

concepts.title: Equations
concepts.content: A mathematical statement that two expressions are equal, containing an unknown variable to solve for. An equation is like a balanced scale - whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other to keep it balanced.

concepts.title: Inequalities
concepts.content: A mathematical statement comparing two expressions using <, >, ≤, or ≥. Inequalities show relationships where one side is greater than, less than, or equal to the other.
concepts.latex: x > 5 \text{ means } x \text{ can be any number greater than 5}

steps: Identify what operation is being done to x: 4 is added to x
Use inverse operation: subtract 4 from both sides
commonErrors: Only subtracting from one side of the equation
Trying to divide first instead of adding/subtracting
Making arithmetic errors in the checking step

practice.explanation: First subtract 3: 2x = 8, then divide by 2: x = 4.

practice.problem: Which inequality symbol means 'greater than or equal to'?
practice.explanation: The symbol ≥ means 'greater than or equal to', combining > and =.
hints: Look for the symbol that combines > and =
